definitionBean.title: Similarity of Triangles
definitionBean.definition: Two triangles are said to be similar if their corresponding angles are equal and their corresponding sides are proportional.
definitionBean.explanation: Similar triangles may have different sizes, but they have the same shape. Criteria like AAA, SSS, SAS are used to prove similarity. The ratio of the areas of two similar triangles is equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides.
importantPoints: Corresponding angles are equal and sides are proportional
AAA, SSS, SAS are criteria of similarity

definitionBean.title: Basic Proportionality Theorem - BPT / Thales Theorem
definitionBean.definition: If a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle to intersect the other two sides in distinct points, the other two sides are divided in the same ratio.
definitionBean.explanation: This theorem is also known as Thales Theorem. It establishes a relationship between parallel lines and ratios in a triangle, and its converse is also true — if a line divides sides in the same ratio, it is parallel to the third side.
importantPoints: Parallel line divides remaining sides in the same ratio

definitionBean.title: Area Theorem for Similar Triangles
definitionBean.definition: The ratio of the areas of two similar triangles is equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides.
definitionBean.explanation: If two triangles are similar and the ratio of their corresponding sides is k, then the ratio of their areas will be k². This theorem is also related to the ratios of altitudes, medians, and perimeters of similar triangles.
importantPoints: Ratio of areas = (Ratio of corresponding sides)²
This also applies to the ratio of altitudes and medians
This theorem is valid only for similar triangles

parts.statement: In the figure, if DE || AC and DF || AE, prove that BF / FE = BE / EC.
parts.explanation:
In triangle ABC, since DE || AC,
By Basic Proportionality Theorem (BPT):
BD / DA = BE / EC  --(Equation 1)

Similarly, in triangle ABE, since DF || AE,
By BPT:
BD / DA = BF / FE  --(Equation 2)

From equations (1) and (2):
BF / FE = BE / EC
Hence proved.

Statement: If a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle intersecting the other two sides in distinct points, then the other two sides are divided in the same ratio.

Proof:
Let a line DE parallel to side BC of ΔABC intersect AB at D and AC at E.
To prove: AD / DB = AE / EC
Construction: Join B to E and C to D, and draw EF ⊥ AB and DG ⊥ AC.

Area of ΔADE = ½ × base × height = ½ × AD × EF
Area of ΔBDE = ½ × BD × EF
Thus area ratio: ar(ΔADE) / ar(ΔBDE) = (½ × AD × EF) / (½ × BD × EF) = AD / DB  --(1)

Similarly, ar(ΔADE) / ar(DEC) = AE / EC  --(2)
Since ΔBDE and ΔDEC are on the same base DE and between the same parallel lines BC and DE, ar(ΔBDE) = ar(ΔDEC).
Thus from equations (1) and (2):
AD / DB = AE / EC
Hence proved.

parts.statement: The areas of two similar triangles are 64 cm² and 121 cm² respectively. If the side of the first triangle is 15.4 cm, find the corresponding side of the second triangle.
parts.explanation:
Let the two similar triangles be ΔABC and ΔPQR.
Given: ar(ΔABC) = 64 cm², ar(ΔPQR) = 121 cm²
AB = 15.4 cm, find PQ.

According to the Area Theorem, the ratio of the areas of two similar triangles is equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides:
ar(ΔABC) / ar(ΔPQR) = (AB / PQ)²
64 / 121 = (15.4 / PQ)²

Taking square root on both sides:
8 / 11 = 15.4 / PQ
PQ = (15.4 × 11) / 8
PQ = 169.4 / 8 = 21.175 cm
Therefore, the corresponding side of the second triangle is 21.175 cm.

parts.statement: Prove that the ratio of the areas of two similar triangles is equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides.
parts.explanation:
Let ΔABC ~ ΔPQR.
To prove: ar(ΔABC) / ar(ΔPQR) = (AB / PQ)² = (BC / QR)² = (CA / RP)²

Construction: Draw altitudes AM ⊥ BC and PN ⊥ QR of the triangles.
ar(ΔABC) / ar(ΔPQR) = [½ × BC × AM] / [½ × QR × PN] = (BC / QR) × (AM / PN)  --(1)

Now in ΔABM and ΔPQN:
∠B = ∠Q (since ΔABC ~ ΔPQR)
∠AMB = ∠PNQ = 90°
Thus by AA similarity, ΔABM ~ ΔPQN
Therefore, AM / PN = AB / PQ  --(2)

Since ΔABC ~ ΔPQR, AB / PQ = BC / QR = CA / RP
Thus from (1) and (2):
ar(ΔABC) / ar(ΔPQR) = (AB / PQ) × (AB / PQ) = (AB / PQ)²
Similarly, it is proved for other sides.
